sense: finish a university degree; one who has

terms.gloss: to graduate, to take a degree
terms.grammar: phrase: adipīscor, adipīscī, adeptus sum, deponent
evidence: M-O s.v. graduate vb. (lauream vel gradum acadēmicum adipīscī)
terms.comment: A modern thing in classical words. A graduate is quī gradum acadēmicum adeptus est (M-O s.v. graduate subst.).

terms.gloss: to graduate (to be given the laurel)
terms.grammar: phrase: passive of dōnō with the ablative
evidence: M-O s.v. graduate vb., citing Vives (1540)
terms.comment: After the laurel of the old degree ceremonies.
Classically a diplōma is an official letter of recommendation or a pass for the public post (Cic.); the degree certificate is modern.

terms.gloss: a graduate; a woman is graduāta
terms.comment: Not in Lewis & Short; formed on medieval gradus, an academic degree.

sources: Lewis & Short: adipiscor · Lewis & Short: laurea · Lewis & Short: diploma
